# Purpose

This log records the onboarding and early-method development work for the UTAS
AGN jet/X-ray cavity project.

The working frame for this exercise is deliberately unusual:

- Barry is playing the role of a beginning Honours student in physics
- the supervisors are Stas Shabala and Patrick Yates-Jones
- Codex is providing structured, agentic workflow support
- the aim is to test how much acceleration and uplift this style of working can
  provide in a real research context

That framing matters. These notes are not just a lab notebook; they are also a
trace of how an assisted research workflow was constructed, what was learned,
and how results were validated.

# Operating Model

The current workflow playbook is:

- WSL laptop as the control plane for planning, editing, review, and launch
- `deep-server` as the preferred execution machine for builds, runs, and
  heavier analysis
- remote tasks written as reusable scripts
- long-running jobs launched inside `tmux`
- outputs synchronized back with `rsync`

The workspace-level instructions are also mirrored in:

- `/home/bwbrook/git/utas-agn/AGENTS.md`
- `/home/bwbrook/git/utas-agn/AGENTS.md` on `deep-server`

# Report Register

## 2026-04-17

- [PLUTO Jet Setup and Basic Jet Simulation](reports/2026-04-17-jet-setup-basic.qmd)
  First direct `jet-setup` onboarding exercise: map the roles of `pluto.ini`, `definitions.h`, `definitions_usr.h`, and `init.c`, then build and run a lightweight 2D spherical King-environment jet case on `deep-server`.
- [PLUTO Basic Jet Parameter Sweep](reports/2026-04-17-jet-parameter-sweep.qmd)
  Small follow-up on the same 2D spherical jet setup, comparing baseline, higher-power, and wider-angle cases to confirm that simple runtime parameter changes produce sensible morphological differences.

## 2026-04-16

- [PLUTO Sod Shock Tube Baseline](reports/2026-04-16-sod-shock-tube.qmd)
  First plain-PLUTO onboarding exercise: build, solver sweep, resolution sweep,
  exact-solution error pass, and initial interpretation.
- [PLUTO Sod Shock Tube with Diffusive Solver Comparison](reports/2026-04-16-sod-diffusive-solvers.qmd)
  Follow-up solver study adding `hll` and `tvdlf`, showing that the contact
  discontinuity is much more sensitive to solver diffusivity than the shock
  position itself.
- [PLUTO Rayleigh-Taylor Instability Scheme Comparison](reports/2026-04-16-rt-instability-schemes.qmd)
  Roe-solver RT study comparing `flat + euler`, `linear + hancock`, and
  `parabolic + rk3`, showing progressively richer interface structure and a
  broader mixed layer for the higher-order schemes.
- [PLUTO Kelvin-Helmholtz Instability Scheme Comparison](reports/2026-04-16-kh-instability-schemes.qmd)
  Custom HD KH study comparing `flat + euler`, `linear + rk2`, and
  `parabolic + rk3`, showing that both higher-order schemes strongly outgrow the
  diffusive baseline, with `linear + rk2` leading the chosen growth metrics in
  this setup.
- [PLUTO Instability Scheme Synthesis for Supervisors](reports/2026-04-16-instability-scheme-synthesis.qmd)
  Supervisor-facing synthesis of the RT and KH onboarding studies, highlighting
  the consistent rejection of `flat + euler` and the more nuanced trade-off
  between the two higher-order schemes.
